source.title: CrossNorm: Normalization for Off-Policy TD Reinforcement Learning
source.authors: Aditya Bhatt; Max J. Argus; Artemij Amiranashvili; Thomas Brox

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper, but its title metadata conflicts with the document: the text is CrossQ, “Batch Normalization in Deep Reinforcement Learning for Greater Sample Efficiency and Simplicity,” published at ICLR 2024.
record.tranche_reason: The paper applies BatchNorm and related normalization choices in off-policy reinforcement learning and reports learning-performance results in a new setting. It does not test training classification error on CIFAR or the other classification claims.
record.gate_note: Results about Q-function normalization, target networks and reinforcement-learning returns bear on the BatchNorm training-speed version in an RL setting. The paper does not measure classification error or whether networks reach zero training error. Cited supervised-learning findings are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study measures off-policy RL episodic returns and sample efficiency, rather than the accuracy-versus-training progress or higher-learning-rate tolerance named in V6. Its normalization ablations establish effects on a related outcome, but do not test any supplied version. The authors' analogy to supervised training acceleration does not supply the missing measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute CrossQ's efficiency to combining BatchNorm with target-network removal, claim training acceleration analogous to supervised learning, and find no straightforward relationship between Q-estimation bias and agent performance. Their reported acceleration is established through RL returns and sample efficiency.
record.recipe_differences: Off-policy actor-critic reinforcement learning with BatchNorm/BRN, target-network removal and wider critics; evaluates episodic returns and sample efficiency rather than classification error.
record.method_sensitivity: Target-network presence changes the BatchNorm outcome; BN versus BRN and the moving-average momentum affect late-training collapses; critic-only versus actor-and-critic normalization has a small reported effect; LayerNorm degrades performance relative to BatchNorm.

fits_no_version.finding: CrossQ matches or surpasses strong continuous-control baselines in sample efficiency using UTD = 1, with environment-dependent advantages.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CrossQ's combined architectural and algorithmic changes improve continuous-control RL sample efficiency at a low update-to-data ratio.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing target networks alone yields small improvements; combining their removal with BatchNorm yields the best aggregate returns, whereas BatchNorm with target networks fails to learn in half the environments.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: BatchNorm's benefit for off-policy RL sample efficiency depends on how target networks and normalization statistics are handled.

fits_no_version.finding: Removing BRN causes divergence; replacing it with LayerNorm lowers returns roughly to SAC performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: CrossQ's stability and return depend on its normalization choice.

fits_no_version.finding: Original BN sometimes collapses later in training; BRN with default or higher momentum avoids these collapses in the tested runs. Critic-only BRN retains strong performance.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Normalization variant, momentum, and placement affect CrossQ's long-run stability and returns.

record.problems: The study is empirical and confined to continuous-control RL; the relevant outcomes are episodic returns and sample efficiency rather than classification training error or accuracy. Several ablation conclusions are qualitative in the text, with exact curve values left to figures. The BatchNorm ablation uses 10 seeds, while the normalization-variant comparison uses five seeds.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were extracted for cited prior-work results. Figure-only numeric points were not reconstructed. Main figures and ablations report RL performance, not classification error; rows were kept only where the result bears on the BatchNorm training-speed version in its RL extension setting.

untested.parts: All: training classification error in convolutional networks, including corrupted labels and model-size or training-recipe conditions.
All: teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and extra student neurons.
All: depth-related training-error degradation, residual shortcuts, special tanh initializations, and Fixup.
All: initialization-dependent training speed, signal propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian weights.
All: learning rates relative to stability thresholds, loss recovery, and curvature dynamics.

Accuracy gains over training relative to unnormalized networks, tolerance of higher learning rates, and normalization-free Fixup training. RL return per environment interaction does not measure these outcomes.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied document is CrossQ, published at ICLR 2024. Related RL outcomes should not receive verdicts on the supplied classification and optimization versions.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error, CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size and training duration.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima and width differences.
Depth, plain versus residual classification networks, ImageNet/CIFAR training error, and the cited special-initialization or Fixup results.
Activation-matched initializations, signal and gradient propagation, trainable depth, and orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization.
Learning rates relative to stability limits, loss curvature and sharpness during gradient descent.
The paper tests BatchNorm-related learning effects in off-policy RL, not classification accuracy on MNIST, CIFAR-10 or ImageNet, tolerance of higher learning rates, or Fixup networks.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with BRN in actor and critic, without target networks, at UTD = 1; evaluated episodic returns during training.

conditions.value: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid, HalfCheetah, HumanoidStandup

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by episodic returns over environment interactions.
rows.baseline: REDQ and DroQ baselines; on Hopper, Walker2d, and HalfCheetah, CrossQ and REDQ learning curves overlap with no significant difference.
rows.value: CrossQ matches or outperforms the best baseline in all presented environments except Ant, where REDQ performs better early and CrossQ eventually matches it; on Humanoid and HumanoidStandup, CrossQ substantially surpasses all baselines.
rows.uncertainty: IQM and 70% quantile intervals over 10 seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: This is an RL return/sample-efficiency outcome, not classification accuracy or training classification error.
rows.check: Compares the complete CrossQ method against different algorithms using RL returns; it neither isolates BatchNorm nor measures V6's accuracy gain.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with tanh critic activations, without target networks and without BatchNorm.

conditions.value: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid, HalfCheetah, HumanoidStandup

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by episodic returns over environment interactions.
rows.value: Removing target networks provides only small improvements over the SAC baseline with target networks.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over 10 seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: The experiment uses tanh so SAC can train without target networks; it does not test classification accuracy.
rows.check: Measures target-network removal without BatchNorm, so cannot establish a BatchNorm effect. Duplicates R9.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh + BN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with tanh critic activations and BatchNorm while retaining target networks.

conditions.value: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid, HalfCheetah, HumanoidStandup

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by episodic returns over environment interactions.
rows.baseline: SAC (tanh) baseline with target networks and without BatchNorm.
rows.value: The combination of BatchNorm and target networks performs inconsistently, failing to learn anything in half of the environments.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over 10 seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: The paper attributes the failure context to this configuration; the specific environments are not named in the text.
rows.check: Reports RL learning failures, not the measure named in V6. The aggregate 'absent' state also obscures mixed results: failure is reported for half the environments.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh − TN + BN)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with tanh critic activations and BatchNorm, with target networks removed.

conditions.value: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid, HalfCheetah, HumanoidStandup

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by episodic returns over environment interactions.
rows.baseline: SAC (tanh) variants with target networks and/or without BatchNorm.
rows.value: The configuration without target networks and with BatchNorm achieves the best aggregate performance; the combination accelerates learning the most.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over 10 seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: The paper calls this configuration the closest to CrossQ; it uses original BatchNorm in this ablation.
rows.check: Measures episodic-return sample efficiency after combining BatchNorm with target-network removal; it does not measure classification accuracy or learning-rate tolerance.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with BRN in actor and critic, without target networks, at UTD = 1.
rows.measure: Percent loss in IQM return relative to CrossQ.
rows.value: Removing the BRN layers proves detrimental and results in the worst overall performance.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: The text does not give the numerical percent loss for this ablation.
rows.check: Subject should be CrossQ without BRN, and operation_detail should describe removing normalization. Appendix Figure 13 explicitly reports training divergence, strengthening the extracted description of poor returns. Neither outcome tests a supplied version.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Trained with LayerNorm replacing BatchNorm in the CrossQ setup.
rows.measure: IQM return relative to CrossQ and SAC baseline.
rows.value: Replacing BatchNorm with LayerNorm degrades CrossQ performance significantly, roughly to the level of the SAC baseline.
rows.uncertainty: 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals in the aggregate ablation figure; numerical values not stated in text.
rows.note: A normalization comparison in RL; not a classification-accuracy result.
rows.check: Subject should be CrossQ with LayerNorm replacing BRN. This compares normalization methods through RL returns, rather than testing V6's named outcome.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Compared BatchNorm variants and moving-average momentums in CrossQ.

conditions.value: BRN, momentum 0.99 (default) versus original BN, moving-average momentum 0.99

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by IQM episodic return over environment interactions.
rows.value: All variants have similar sample efficiency in early training; original BN is prone to sudden performance collapses during longer runs, while BRN with default and higher momentums shows no collapses.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over five seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: The paper reports a late-training stability difference between BN and BRN, despite comparable early sample efficiency.
rows.check: Compares BN and BRN stability without an unnormalized control. Comparable early returns and occasional later collapses cannot determine BatchNorm's acceleration relative to no normalization.

rows.subject: CrossQ (ours)
rows.operation_detail: Compared using BRN only in the critic with BRN in both actor and critic.
rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by IQM episodic return over environment interactions.
rows.baseline: BRN in both actor and critic.
rows.value: Using BatchNorm only in the critic is sufficient to drive strong performance; including it in both networks performs slightly better.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over five seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: The text gives a qualitative comparison; it does not state numerical return differences.
rows.check: Subject should be CrossQ with BRN only in the critic. The caption says omitting actor normalization has no significant effect; a slightly lower return does not establish a partial BatchNorm acceleration effect.

rows.subject: SAC (tanh)
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAC with and without target networks, using tanh activations to avoid divergence.

conditions.value: Hopper, Walker2d, Ant, Humanoid, HalfCheetah, HumanoidStandup

rows.measure: Sample efficiency, measured by episodic returns over environment interactions.
rows.value: SAC without target networks supports the common intuition that target networks slow learning to a small extent.
rows.uncertainty: IQM return and 70% quantile intervals over 10 seeds; no numerical interval values stated in text.
rows.note: This result concerns removing target networks, not BatchNorm itself.
rows.check: Duplicates R2 and should be merged with it. Target-network removal without BatchNorm does not test V6.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CrossQ and SAC ablations in the tested off-policy continuous-control RL environments
reader_labels.reason: BatchNorm with target networks failed to learn in half of the environments, while the no-target-network BatchNorm configuration performed best; the paper's BN/BRN variants also differed in late-run stability (R3, R4, R7). These RL return results do not establish faster classification accuracy on the datasets named in V6.
